howto.goal: Checkmate the other king: put it in check with no legal way out.
howto.setup: The usual starting position. White moves first.

sections.title: Pieces
sections.text: Each piece moves its own way. Pawns go forward one square, or two on their first move, and capture diagonally.

sections.title: Check and mate
sections.text: A king in check must escape. If it cannot, the game is over — checkmate.

sections.title: Castling
sections.text: Once your king and rook are untouched, click the king and then two squares toward the rook to castle.

sections.title: Draws
sections.text: Stalemate, fifty moves with no capture or pawn move, threefold repetition, and too little material to mate are draws.

controls: Click a piece, then the square it should move to.
Legal destinations are marked when a piece is picked up.
Promotion and castling happen by clicking the two squares; a small chooser appears for a pawn reaching the last rank.

frames.say: A pawn may go two squares from its start.
A knight jumps in an L shape.
Castling moves the king two squares.

demo.intro: A short opening played by the computer, with the ideas named as they happen.

lines.say: The starting position. White moves first.
White pushes the king's pawn two squares and opens the centre.
Black mirrors it, claiming the same central squares.
White develops a knight toward the centre.
Black develops a knight to defend the centre pawn.
White's bishop aims at the weakest square in black's camp.
Black defends it and prepares to castle.

demo.outro: In the opening, develop your pieces and keep your king safe. Do not chase pawns with your queen.

steps.say: Click the pawn in front of your king, then two squares forward.
Bring a knight out toward the centre — knights jump in an L shape.
Develop your bishop so it aims at the other side's weak square.
Castle to keep your king safe: click the king, then two squares toward the rook.
